activityGoals.name: Creating an Array of Odd Numbers
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that creates an array of first ten positive odd numbers.

lineList.content: //Step 1: Create an array of ten elements of type int

commentList: We need to create an array that could hold 10 odd numbers. This statement declares an array variable, lst, creates an array of ten elements of int type, and assigns its reference to lst. By default, each number in an int array is 0.

lineList.content: //Step 2: Iterate over the indexes of the array

commentList: We use a for loop to iterate over the array indexes and set an odd value to each index. We need the array indexes to have a length of 10 and start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every integer number up to but not including 10.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less than 10 (array length) and terminates when the control variable reaches 10 (array length). In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
Also, note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.

lineList.content: //Step 2.1: Assign an odd number to the index i of the array

commentList: We want to add an odd value to each index. To do this, in each iteration, we set 2*i+1 to the element at the index i of the array. Note that 2*i+1 is always an odd number.

To print the array elements, we need to traverse the array and then print each element as we visit it. We traverse the array elements using for–each statement. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
